question: Supplier S-103 will miss its next RM-103 shipment by four weeks. Handle it.
answer:
I raised a purchase requisition with the backup supplier for one of the two affected plants. Oculon, made at the other plant, has no approved backup and will get its next resupply about 4 weeks late. No allocation is needed yet because Oculon stock is above safety stock at every distribution centre (DC). This run was flagged for human review: the alternate supplier covers only one of the two plants, and the process (Supply Disruption Response) has no path for that. No trusted or discovery playbook matched either.

**What I found**
- **The late order:** S-103 (Castellan Excipients) is late on order PO000210 for 3,300 units of RM-103 (Glycerin USP). It was promised for 2026-10-03 and will now ship around 2026-10-31. S-103 has four more open orders for RM-103 (PO000211 to PO000213, due 10-10 to 10-25), and I haven't confirmed whether those will slip too.
- **Affected products:** I walked the current bill of materials with trace_supply_exposure. RM-103 feeds Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL (FG-1001/1002) and Cyclosporine 0.05% 5 mL (FG-1003), all made at plant PL-01. It also feeds Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL (FG-2001/2002), made at plant PL-02.
- **Backup supplier:** S-111 (Kingsley Excipients) is qualified for RM-103 and active, but the supplier portal approves it to ship to PL-01 only. PL-02 has no approved backup.
- **Stock (latest snapshot, 2026-09-25):**
  - All three Oculon pack/DC combinations are above safety stock, so the process says no allocation is needed yet.
  - On hand covers only about 31–51 days of shipments: Oculon 5 mL at DC-WEST about 31 days, Oculon 2.5 mL at DC-CENTRAL about 35 days.
- **When supply recovers:** It takes 46 days from the material shipping to Oculon reaching the DCs, including the 14-day sterility test. The delayed batch should reach DCs around 2026-12-16 instead of around 2026-11-18. So Oculon could drop below safety stock in November or December.
- **Substitutes:** Oculon has no approved company substitute. Cyclosporine OS, the approved substitute for Lacrivia, is fed by the same material, but PL-01 is covered by the backup supplier.
- **Customers:** All five contracted health systems have Oculon prescriptions in the last 13 weeks at all three DCs. Six wholesalers receive Oculon: W-01 and W-02 from DC-EAST, W-03 and W-04 from DC-CENTRAL, W-05 and W-06 from DC-WEST.

**What I did**
1. **Purchase requisition PR-862E69EF:** 3,300 units of RM-103 from S-111, shipped to PL-01, needed by 2026-10-03, to be expedited.
2. **CASE-E9A8DB23 to Procurement / Supplier Quality:** asks them to expedite or split-ship S-103's PL-02 share, confirm the later S-103 orders, and look at urgently approving S-111 to ship to PL-02.
3. **CASE-2692E02B to the Supply Planning lead:** asks for a review of how I handled the partial coverage, and for the allocation step to be re-run on the next weekly snapshots. It also flags the Lacrivia DC-EAST shortage described below.
4. **CASE-3602D8EB to Trade Relations:** asks them to send the delay notice to wholesalers W-01 to W-06. The wholesaler EDI tool isn't available, so the process sends this to Trade Relations.
5. **CRM tasks for the account teams:** each says there is no allocation, gives the expected mid-December recovery, says Oculon has no approved substitute (refer to Medical Affairs) and that Lacrivia and Cyclosporine OS are not expected to be affected.
   - Tier A: Northfield (CRM-DFF198EC), Oak Hollow (CRM-404E672C), Riverbend (CRM-1B5C8AEA)
   - Tier B: Clearview (CRM-06595D5F), Sunridge (CRM-593FB5A2)

**What I did not do**
- **No allocation or approval request:** No Oculon pack is below safety stock. Lacrivia and Cyclosporine aren't cut off because the backup supplier covers PL-01.
- **Lacrivia at DC-EAST:** Lacrivia 5 mL (46 on hand vs 471 safety stock) and 10 mL (34 vs 233) are already below safety stock at DC-EAST. That shortage existed before this slip, so I didn't allocate it as part of this disruption. It is flagged in CASE-2692E02B.
- **No wholesaler inventory check:** that data feed isn't live until Q4 2026.

**Assumptions**
- I sized the requisition at the full late order (3,300 units) because the data doesn't show how much RM-103 each plant uses.
- I treated PL-02 as using RM-103 through CMP-320, because S-103 is approved to ship RM-103 to PL-02.
- The 4-week slip applies to PO000210 only.

**Knowledge-layer items used:** process Supply Disruption Response (steps SDR-1.1 to SDR-4.2); rules BR-ALLOC-01/02, BR-APPR-01, BR-SUB-01/02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-CUST-01 and BR-REGION-01; reference sets supply_contracts, dc_service_regions and approved_substitutes; and the trace_supply_exposure and get_lead_times results.

sql.sql: SELECT PO_ID, SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, ORDER_DT, PROMISED_SHIP_DT, ACTUAL_SHIP_DT, QTY, STATUS FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD WHERE MATERIAL_ID='RM-103' AND (STATUS='OPEN' OR ORDER_DT >= '2026-01-01') ORDER BY PROMISED_SHIP_DT
SELECT sm.SUPPLIER_ID, s.SUPPLIER_NM, s.TIER, sm.QUALIFIED_FLG, sm.PRIMARY_FLG FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=sm.SUPPLIER_ID WHERE sm.MATERIAL_ID='RM-103'

SELECT pm.PLANT_ID, pm.MATERIAL_ID FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL pm WHERE pm.MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-103','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','CMP-320','SEMI-060','FILL-1001','FILL-1002','FILL-1003','FILL-2001','FILL-2002','FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') ORDER BY pm.PLANT_ID, pm.MATERIAL_ID

SELECT b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, b.QTY_PER, b.EFF_FROM, b.EFF_TO, m.MATERIAL_TYP FROM dbo.BOM b JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID WHERE b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-103','CMP-320') OR b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID='CMP-320'
SELECT sm.SUPPLIER_ID, sm.MATERIAL_ID, sm.QUALIFIED_FLG, sm.PRIMARY_FLG FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm WHERE sm.MATERIAL_ID IN ('CMP-320','SEMI-060','SEMI-044','SEMI-045');
SELECT SUPPLIER_ID, SUPPLIER_NM, COUNTRY, TIER FROM dbo.SUPPLIER WHERE SUPPLIER_ID IN ('S-103','S-111','S-202','S-203')
SELECT PLANT_ID, COUNT(*) n, SUM(CASE WHEN MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'RM-%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) rm, SUM(CASE WHEN MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'CMP-%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cmp FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL GROUP BY PLANT_ID

SELECT i.DC_ID, i.MATERIAL_ID, i.SNAPSHOT_DT, i.ON_HAND_UNITS, i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV i WHERE i.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND i.SNAPSHOT_DT = (SELECT MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) FROM dbo.DC_INV i2 WHERE i2.DC_ID=i.DC_ID AND i2.MATERIAL_ID=i.MATERIAL_ID) ORDER BY i.MATERIAL_ID, i.DC_ID

SELECT s.DC_ID, s.MATERIAL_ID, SUM(s.UNITS) units_28d, SUM(s.UNITS)/28.0 avg_daily, MAX(s.SHIP_DT) last_ship FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s WHERE s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND s.SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-28,'2026-09-30') GROUP BY s.DC_ID, s.MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY s.MATERIAL_ID, s.DC_ID

WITH wks AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
acct AS (SELECT a.ACCOUNT_ID, a.STATE, COALESCE(gp.ACCOUNT_ID, p.ACCOUNT_ID, a.ACCOUNT_ID) TOP_ID FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT p ON a.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID=p.ACCOUNT_ID LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT gp ON p.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID=gp.ACCOUNT_ID)
SELECT CASE WHEN ac.STATE IN ('IL','TX','MN','CO') THEN 'DC-CENTRAL' WHEN ac.STATE IN ('NY','NJ','PA','MA','FL','GA','NC','OH') THEN 'DC-EAST' WHEN ac.STATE IN ('AZ','CA','WA') THEN 'DC-WEST' ELSE 'OTHER' END DC, ac.TOP_ID, t.ACCOUNT_NM, r.PROD_NDC11, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) TRX13
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wks ON r.WK_END_DT=wks.WK_END_DT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER pr ON pr.PRSCRBR_ME=r.PRSCRBR_ME JOIN acct ac ON ac.ACCOUNT_ID=pr.ACCOUNT_ID JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT t ON t.ACCOUNT_ID=ac.TOP_ID
WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101030325','99101030350') AND ac.TOP_ID IN ('AC00117','AC00038','AC00059','AC00001','AC00138')
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 1,2,4

SELECT s.WHSLR_ID, w.*, s.DC_ID, SUM(s.UNITS) units_13wk FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s JOIN dbo.WHSLR w ON w.WHSLR_ID=s.WHSLR_ID WHERE s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-2001','FG-2002') AND s.SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-91,'2026-09-30') GROUP BY s.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_NM, s.DC_ID ORDER BY s.DC_ID, s.WHSLR_ID

escalation_cases.subject: RM-103 (Glycerin USP) for PL-02: S-103 4-week slip, no approved alternate for PL-02
escalation_cases.details: S-103 Castellan Excipients will miss RM-103 PO000210 (3,300 units, promised 2026-10-03) by ~4 weeks (new ship ~2026-10-31). Open S-103 POs PO000211/212/213 (promised 10-10, 10-18, 10-25) should be confirmed as well. Alternate S-111 Kingsley Excipients is qualified and active but approved in the supplier portal for PL-01 ONLY; a PR (PR-862E69EF, 3,300 units) was raised with S-111 for PL-01. PL-02 (Oculon: RM-103 -> CMP-320 -> SEMI-060 -> FILL-2001/2002 -> FG-2001/FG-2002) has no qualified alternate. Requested: (1) expedite / partial shipment from S-103 for the PL-02 portion of PO000210; (2) assess urgent site approval of S-111 RM-103 for PL-02 (or supply via CMP-320 suppliers S-202/S-203 if they source glycerin independently). Recovery lead time RM-103 -> Oculon at DC is 46 days (get_lead_times, incl. 14-day sterility), so the delayed lot reaches DCs ~2026-12-16 instead of ~2026-11-18.

escalation_cases.subject: S-103/RM-103 slip: partial alternate coverage (PL-01 only) - review and Oculon stock watch
escalation_cases.details: Process SDR-2.1 decision has no branch for an alternate approved for only some plants: S-111 covers PL-01 (Lacrivia FG-1001/1002, Cyclosporine FG-1003; PR-862E69EF raised) but not PL-02 (Oculon FG-2001/2002). Handled as: PL-01 packs treated as covered (no allocation per BR-ALLOC-02); PL-02 Oculon packs treated as interrupted. Latest DC_INV snapshot 2026-09-25: Oculon above safety stock at all DCs (FG-2001 C 293/120, E 417/180, W 268/100; FG-2002 C 109/46, E 177/70, W 77/38) -> no allocation needed now (SDR-2.4). But days of supply on hand are only ~31-51 days (FG-2002 West ~31d, FG-2001 Central ~35d) and the delayed lot reaches DCs ~2026-12-16 (46-day lead time), so Oculon may fall below safety stock in Nov-Dec: please re-run the allocation step (BR-ALLOC-01/02, BR-APPR-01) on the next weekly snapshots. Oculon has no approved company substitute (BR-SUB-01). Separately FYI: Lacrivia FG-1001 (46 vs SS 471) and FG-1002 (34 vs SS 233) are already below safety stock at DC-EAST - pre-existing, not caused by this slip since S-111 covers PL-01; not allocated under this disruption. Run flagged for human review (no trusted playbook).
